headline: Oilers activate Zach Hyman, Devon Levi off IR
take:
Edmonton gets two pieces back at once: Daily Faceoff reports the Oilers have activated Zach Hyman and Devon Levi off injured reserve after about two weeks out.

Hyman matters most. He scored 31 goals in 58 games last season, much of it from the dirty areas beside Connor McDavid, and he has only one goal in seven games this year on 2.1 expected goals (the quality of his chances). That shortfall is small and should close. The Oilers haven't needed him much: they're 12-3-3 and have scored 19.39 more goals than their chances usually produce, which is the kind of finishing that tends to cool. Hyman's return is a hedge against that.

Levi, 7-1-0 with a .890 save rate and slightly below expected (-1.11), gives Edmonton its goaltending depth back. His high-danger save rate (.750 against a league .810) is the number we'd watch.
